title: Moong Dal Vada / Gâteau Piment
subtitle: Fried lentil fritters, two ways — Indian moong dal vada or Mauritian gâteau piment.
protein: ~10–12g protein per adult serving — from moong dal or split peas

nightPrep.label: Night Before — pick your version
items: Indian moong dal vada: soak 1 cup yellow moong dal (split, skinned) 2–3 hours
Mauritian gâteau piment: soak 1 cup yellow split peas 8–12 hours — they need much longer
Drain well before grinding

items.name: Moong dal or split peas, soaked

method.title: Grind the base
items: Drain the soaked dal or split peas {1 cup} well — split peas feel firmer than dal even after a long soak
Add to a blender with ginger {1 tbsp} and a pinch of the salt

Pulse to a coarse, thick paste — no added water; batter should hold its shape on a spoon. Split peas grind a bit coarser than moong dal — a few small flecks are normal and give gâteau piment its characteristic bite.
Transfer to a mixing bowl

method.title: Season the base
items: Mix in hing {¼ tsp}, cumin seeds {1 tsp}, crushed coriander seeds {1 tsp}, and turmeric {¼ tsp}
Mix in remaining salt to taste
This is the shared base — no chili has gone in yet

method.label: Toddler portion — pull now
items: Scoop out about ⅓ cup of the seasoned base into a separate bowl before any chili is added
Fold in mashed potato {3 tbsp} and ghee {1 tsp} to soften the texture
Set aside — this bowl stays out of all remaining adult steps

method.title: Spice the adult batter
items: Into the remaining base, mix in green chili {1–2}, and your chosen herb — curry leaves {10 leaves} for the Indian version, or fresh thyme {1 tbsp} for Mauritian — plus cilantro {3 tbsp}
Mix evenly — this is now the adult batter only

method.title: Shape and fry the adult batch
items: Heat oil in a kadai or heavy pot over medium-high heat
Wet hands, shape adult batter into small flat patties {~2 tbsp each} — for gâteau piment, shape slightly thicker in the center than a typical vada
Fry in batches until deep golden and firm — 3–4 minutes per side for moong dal, 4–5 minutes for split peas, which take a little longer to cook through
Drain on a rack or paper towel

method.title: Cook the toddler patties
items: Heat ghee {1 tbsp} in a small nonstick pan over medium-low heat
Shape the toddler batter into 3–4 small, thin patties (thinner than the adult ones, for a soft bite)
Pan-sear 2–3 minutes per side until set through and lightly golden — no raw batter should remain
Cool and cut into soft strips before serving to reduce choking risk

method.label: About this recipe
method.text: These are culinary cousins — both trace back to Indian indentured-labor cooking traditions, but diverged: Indian moong dal vada uses skinned split mung bean and curry leaves; Mauritian gâteau piment traditionally uses yellow split peas and thyme (often chives too, swapped here for cilantro to stay onion/garlic-free for Jain). Toor dal isn't offered as a third option — it's too soft and crumbly to hold together fried this way; it's better suited to dal fry or sambar. Texture check: batter should hold together without added water — too wet, add a spoon of chickpea flour; too dry, add a few drops of water at a time.

method.label: Appliance & storage
method.text: Stovetop kadai works best for the adult batch either way. For a lighter version in the Ninja Crispi, brush patties with oil and air-fry at 350°F for 8–10 minutes, flipping halfway — add 2–3 minutes for the split-pea version, and check a bit early since the Crispi runs hot. Toddler patties stay stovetop pan-seared, not air-fried; their thin shape dries out fast in the Crispi. Leftover vadas keep 3 days refrigerated and re-crisp nicely in a dry pan, or the Crispi at 330°F for 3–4 minutes.
